newsitem.title: UK: Offer sees opening UK electric market in April '98.
newsitem.headline: Offer sees opening UK electric market in April '98.

text.p: British electricity industry regulator Offer said on Thursday a number of utilities would be ready for the opening of Britain's electricity market to full competition in April 1998.
"April 1998 remains achievable for a number of companies, but not all," said Stephen Littlechild, director general of Electricity Supply, in a statement.
Offer said three Public Electricity Suppliers (PESs) -- Eastern Electricity, Seeboard, and Yorkshire Electricity -- should be ready for the April target date.
The pool that facilitates the trading of electricity between generators and suppliers should also meet the start date, Offer said.
All 14 PESs, possibly barring Southern Electric Plc, should be ready to open their markets between April and July, Offer said.
"Southern still have some way to go in getting their systems ready. However, they may be ready to go (in April)," an Offer spokeswoman said.
The regulator said it planned to slap penalties on companies that entered the market late.
"The introduction of competition across the country should not be dictated by the pace of the slowest company," Littlechild said.

"This would not be reasonable either for customers or for those companies ready on time. Such companies should not be required to incur costs while waiting for slower companies to catch up," he added.
The opening of Britain's electricity market will allow companies to expand outside their home regions.

Eastern Electricity is part of the Energy Group, while Seeboard is owned by U.S. firm Central & South West Corp, and Yorkshire is a unit of American Electric Power Co Inc and Public Service Co of Colorado.
Southern Electric is Britain's last remaining independent regional electricity company after its 11 peers were bought.
